auditors.confidence_note: Source only; verified all reads come from history[-1] (the just-closed bar at actionable time) and session-relative bar counts, with no access to scorer, dataset, split, or future-dated state — but I cannot inspect the harness's per-bar view to independently confirm history[-1] excludes the forming bar.

The gate, BH/Holm diagnostics, and deflation margin all agree the result is unexceptional (p=0.237, 0 discoveries, margin -0.093), denominators are healthy (384 sessions, 298 downside, 428 trades), and no p-value sits at the resolution floor; I cannot see how many prior campaigns ran, but since nothing was accepted here that ambiguity is moot for this axis.

reasons: The strategy never constructs a volume profile. The only thing it calls a 'level' is `round(price*4)/4` in `_is_near_natural_level` — the 0.25-point NQ tick grid. The hypothesis explicitly states 'It must condition on a level built from traded volume. A rule that would behave the same with the levels deleted is answering a different question.' This rule would: on tick-quoted NQ data closes already sit on the 0.25 grid, and the 0.50-point proximity tolerance is wide enough to accept essentially any close, so the 'level' filter is vacuous.

No point of control, value area, high-volume node or low-volume node is computed anywhere in the code. `current.volume` and `current.delta` are read only to compute `delta_ratio` for a single bar; nothing aggregates traded volume across bars or carries any level across sessions. The campaign's central construct is absent from the winning strategy.

The initiation question — the explicitly stated second half of the hypothesis — is not answered. Every entry is routed through the pending-setup mechanism, so the strategy ALWAYS waits for a confirming bar and can never take absorption alone. Every fill is tagged `tag="absorption"`, so the record cannot distinguish 'absorption alone' from 'after confirming bar'. The hypothesis requires 'Every entry fill must carry a tag saying whether it was taken on absorption alone or after a confirming bar' and 'It must report what waiting for initiation cost or earned ... including the stop distance at entry both ways'. Neither is done.

Holding period is ~25 minutes (avg_holding_period_ns ≈ 1.52e9 ns ≈ 25.4 min at 5m bars) and 428 round turns over 384 sessions ≈ 1.1 per session. This is the same-session, high-round-turn shape the hypothesis explicitly excludes: 'It must hold for a move between levels. A rule doing many round turns a session for small moves has already been tried four times and is not what this asks.' The stated floor is meant to be met by multi-session holds toward the next level, not by same-session scalping.

The module docstring is entirely about defeating byte-identity in the synthetic evaluation harness via session-phase bar filtering (early/mid/late wick multipliers and 'confirming bar must occur in the same session phase'). None of this bears on the economics of absorption at carried volume levels; it is a search-process artifact made into a strategy filter. The claimed developed hypothesis has drifted off the registered question entirely.

Direction convention is at odds with the stated absorption mechanism. Absorption is defined as 'aggressive one-way flow ... and price does not go anywhere' — i.e. flow that failed to move price. Here `delta > 0` (net aggressive buying for the whole bar) plus a lower wick yields a long, and `delta < 0` plus an upper wick yields a short: the delta is bar-wide and is not restricted to the region of the tail where the failure supposedly occurred, so the rule is a bar-shape + bar-delta heuristic, not a test of flow-that-failed at a level.

Breadth is genuinely broad across all three time dimensions (11/17 months, 4/6 weekdays, 12/19 hours positive) with low single-session concentration (best_session_share 3.9%, top-5% concentration 27%), though nearly all net profit arises from Aug–Dec 2025 after a net loss of ~80 over the prior 12 months; without strategy parameters, market-regime context, or out-of-sample validation, I could not determine whether that recent-month dominance reflects regime dependence or legitimate strategy behavior.
